# SVDB merge spike fixture

Four synthetic VCFs backing the design spike that pinned SVDB's merge behaviours.

**These are hand-written INPUTS, not captured svdb output.** Nothing here was generated by a
merge, so an svdb version bump cannot invalidate them —
[`test_svdb_assumptions.py`](../../test_svdb_assumptions.py) re-runs every merge into a temp
directory against whatever `svdb` is on `PATH` and never writes back here. `axisA_SAMP1.vcf` and
`axisB_cohort.vcf` below are outputs you produce locally; they are deliberately not checked in.

First written 2026-07-30 against SVDB 2.8.1. Now asserted against **SVDB 2.12.0**, which is what
`environment.yml`, `tests/Dockerfile` and `modules/merge/svdb_merge.nf` all pin; the suite passes
under it with these fixtures unchanged.

| File | Samples | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `manta_SAMP1.vcf` | SAMP1 | axis-A input: shared chr1 DEL, plus a manta-only DUP and DEL |
| `delly_SAMP1.vcf` | SAMP1 | axis-A input: the same chr1 DEL at shifted breakpoints (0.99 reciprocal overlap), plus a delly-only artifact on chr3 |
| `joint.vcf` | SAMP1, SAMP2 | axis-B input: joint-called, holds the same chr1 DEL and a joint-only chr4 DEL with a `0/0` to check it stays distinct from `./.` |
| `samp3.vcf` | SAMP3 | axis-B input: a chr1 DEL overlapping the joint one — **the genotype-fill test**, since this input loses the cluster to the joint VCF |

`hdr.txt` is the shared header the four files were built from.

## Reproducing

```bash
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/d -w /d quay.io/biocontainers/svdb:2.12.0--py312hfcd9dac_0 svdb --merge --vcf manta_SAMP1.vcf:manta delly_SAMP1.vcf:delly --priority manta,delly --ins_distance 25 > axisA_SAMP1.vcf
```

```bash
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/d -w /d quay.io/biocontainers/svdb:2.12.0--py312hfcd9dac_0 svdb --merge --vcf joint.vcf:jointcaller axisA_SAMP1.vcf:samp1set samp3.vcf:samp3set --priority jointcaller,samp1set,samp3set --ins_distance 25 > axisB_cohort.vcf
```

Expected at `chr1:1000` in `axisB_cohort.vcf`: one record, three columns, `SAMP1 0/1`, `SAMP2 1/1`,
`SAMP3 0/1`. Also expected — and still present until the pipeline fixes it — `svdb_origin`,
`FOUNDBY`, `SUPP_VEC`, `set` and `VARID` each appear **twice** in that record's INFO, and
`bcftools query` returns the first (axis-A) value of each.

The assertions above are automated in [`tests/test_svdb_assumptions.py`](../../test_svdb_assumptions.py):

```bash
conda activate annotate-svs && python tests/test_svdb_assumptions.py
```

Run it after any SVDB upgrade. A failure means a plan assumption no longer holds, and the failure
message names the section to read.

This fixture is the seed of the Phase 2 fixture — grow it rather than starting a new one.
